7.text: Bank of America expects 7–8% net interest income growth and a 36.4% investment-banking fee jump, with its stock up 17.4% over six months. JPMorgan is barely mentioned; the articles cover Bank of America, a peer whose results set the tone for the sector's earnings season.

5.text: JPMorgan will report Q3 earnings next month, with analysts expecting double-digit profit growth; HSBC raised its price target to $377 while keeping a Hold. The stock closed at $336.59, down 1.89%, and sits 6% below its high.

4.text: Jamie Dimon proposed a sweeping US–Europe free trade pact to counter China, conditional on Europe fixing its capital markets, while JPMorgan co-founded Michigan's LIFT initiative. JPMorgan also tweaked fintech data-sharing notices, explored private-credit card lending, weighed a $3.8B Extell construction loan, and doubled down on diesel.

8.text: JPMorganChase partnered with Ford, Michigan, and Newlab to launch Michigan LIFT, an industrial innovation and manufacturing initiative. Other articles cover BlackRock tokenization, credit card perks, Fed oversight thresholds, and unrelated deals, with no further JPMorgan developments.

9.text: JPMorgan upgraded CoreWeave, Bureau Veritas, and Nordnet, cut Monday.com to Neutral, lowered AutoZone's price target while staying positive, and said the tech sell-off has run its course. The Quanta Services article cites Bernstein, not JPMorgan.

6.text: JPMorgan announced a ~$200M sustainable forestry investment in Paraguay, launched a Chase Data Security Center, and is in talks to lead $3.8B construction financing for a Manhattan tower. It also plans to double its GIFT City India business and expanded cross-border payments via a Thunes partnership; Rollins merely held a fireside chat at its conference.
